text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Dutch Rail, trading firm Internatio Mueller, tank storage group Pakhoed have option until Dec 1, 1997 to bid for 30 pct Nedlloyd stake in container transshipment firm ECT. (p1)
- Two major shareholders in Klene Holding sell their 83 pct stake in the sweets company. (p1)
- Publisher Wegener Arcade to buy remaining two thirds of shares in regional daily Provinciale Zeeuwse Courant. (p1)
- Joint property investment firm, launched by insurer Aegon and pension fund PGGM, aims for eight pct annual return. (p1)
- Delft Instruments sells its measuring and testing equipment making unit Kipp & Zonen to Canada's SCI-Tec Inc. (p3)
- Foods and beverages concern BolsWessanen enters Asian market via Thai joint venture. (p3)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- ING bank puts pressure on its staff to accept 40-hour working week instead of 36 hours as agreed in deal on pay and conditions for banking sector. (p1)
- Transport group Nedlloyd sells its 35 pct stake in money and valuables transport unit Brink's Nedlloyd to Brink. (p2)
- Finance Ministry's securities trade watchdog doubles its staff to increase supervision. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Dutch navy boards Dutch fishing boat off Moroccan coast and seizes hashish worth 80 million guilders. (p1)
- Purchasing power of Dutch consumers was nearly one pct higher in 1995 than in previous year. (p53)
- Return on investment in Dutch shares was 37 pct this year. (p55)
- Shipbuilder Koninklijke Schelde Groep wins vital order for two multi-purpose freighters. (p57)
TROUW
- Quarrel between KLM Royal Dutch Airlines and its U.S. partner Northwest Airlines subsides. (p6)
- Central Bank worried about rapidly rising house prices. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Three teenagers, 13, 15 and 17 years old, admit to having murdered a 41-year old woman. (p1)
- Transport concern De Haan is looking for a strong partner before the end of the year so it can stay in business. (p15)
-- Amsterdam newsdesk +31 20 504 5000
